Key.English: Map, compass, watch, radio and GPS
Very heavy rifles and machine guns
Bandages, injectors and small infusions (10 to a tile)
Heavy infusions and blood bags (2 to a tile)
Sutures, cable ties and earplugs (20 to a tile)
Rations, splints, bigger infusions and first aid kits (5 to a tile)

Realistic sizes: long rifles, magazines a tile or two, backpacks with big tiles. Nothing stacks but bandages, injectors, infusions, rations and first aid kits; containers get the room their load gives.

How much load one grid cell stands for,
in the same mass units as the inventory.

Every container gets its maximum load
divided by this as cells. At 5, a
backpack that holds 280 gets 56 cells:
seven rows of eight.

Lower values make bigger grids. Items
keep their size either way.

cell= in the rules text beats this. The
setup wizard's General page sets that.

How big items are, how many share a
tile and how containers are split into
compartments - one text for everyone.

Rules are separated by commas: what a
rule is for, then what it sets. Later
rules beat earlier ones:
kind=grenade > stack=3,
class=ACE_fieldDressing+ > stack=20,
@vest > grid=rig

weight=1.5 and name=Field_kit give an
item a weight in kg and a name.

grid=xxx/x-x draws a compartment cell
by cell, - is a hole. like=CLASS takes
size, stack, grid and rule weight from
another class.

all kind=uniform > grid=5x5 gives every
uniform that has no rule of its own that
size - the setup wizard's General page
writes such rules.

The first part, einv1 base=default
cell=5, names the default the rules build
on and the load per cell. The setup
wizard writes all of this for you.

What cannot be read is left out and
named in the RPT. Empty is the default.

How many cells an item takes, across
and down, for the classes listed here.
Beats the rules text, the item's own
mod and the default rules.

Format: class:WxH, separated by commas.
1x2 is one cell across, two down:
rhs_mag_30Rnd_556x45_M855A1_Stanag:1x2,
rhsusf_100Rnd_762x51:1x3

A class also covers every class that
inherits from it; the nearest one listed
wins. At most 8 across and 40 down.

The rules text does the same and more:
class=rhsusf_100Rnd_762x51+ > size=1x3

Entries that do not read are left out
and named in the RPT.

How many small items share one tile:
the group @item_small in the rules,
everything of a weight up to 10 that is
not a magazine or a weapon.

Nothing stacks by default but a list of
consumables (bandages, injectors,
infusions, rations). Moved off 10, this
stacks every small item that many to a
tile - unless a rule, the stack table or
the item's own mod says otherwise.

Counts only when moved off 10.

How many of an item share one tile, for
the classes listed here. Beats the rules
text, the item's own mod and the
default rules.

Format: class:N, separated by commas:
ACE_fieldDressing:20, ACE_morphine:5

A class also covers every class that
inherits from it; the nearest one listed
wins. ACE_ItemCore:10 stacks every ACE
item by ten, 1 stops an item stacking.

Uniforms, vests, backpacks and weapons
never stack, whatever is listed here.

Entries that do not read are left out
and named in the RPT.
Arma Inventory Overhaul: this machine reads the inventory rules differently from the server - use the server's version of the mod.
Arma Inventory Overhaul %1 here, %2 on the server - item sizes and grids may not match.
